teaches: Retrieval of skills already taught: a short sheet of 5 to 30 problems drawn from the grades and maths areas the teacher ticks, each problem in its own skill's cell at review supports (PT-REV-2), numbered 1..N, scored, with a facsimile answer key and a key summary by area and skill. On screen the same N problems play as a practice card, an online worksheet, a scored quiz and the boss / race games.
summary: A new page type that is a CONFIGURATION of the mixed-practice engine, not a second engine: a pure pool / deal module turns the teacher's filters (grades, areas, only 8/10 skills, unticked skills, from my lessons) and a seed into an explicit list of N items {categoryId, skillId, opts, seed}; buildSheet lays that list out with mixed-practice.js in review mode; every screen host plays the same list. A share code carries the list, the counts, the order and the seed, so the mix is reproduced exactly.
research: No premium logins this round (the card writer has no browser). From knowledge of the reference sites: MathWorksheets4Kids 'mixed review' / 'spiral review' grade packs (a fixed mix of 10-20 items across strands per page, an answer key), K5 Learning 'mixed operations' and grade-level 'review' worksheets, IXL's 'recommendations' and 'skill plans' (screen-side choice of weak skills, per-skill score report), Math-Drills mixed-operation sheets (seeded 'new set' button). Converted to our design: 6-12 problems a page, not 30-50 (12.1); one boxed cell per problem in its own skill's cell; numbers, not letters (PT-MIX-7); the pupil page never names the area (ruling 13). The research must be repeated with the logins before the build (CLAUDE.md MANDATORY step) by lane MR-B.
problemTypes: No new problem type: each item is its own skill's cell at level 1 (PT-REV-2) with its own instruction in the cell or its band strip (PT-MIX-4, PT-MIX-5).

The mix (page-aware deal, dealReviewItems, §7a): pages and their item counts n_p come from §3; a page holds at most 3 distinct skills (12.1 Review: 2–3 instruction-led sections), s_p = max(1, min(3, floor(n_p / 2))); each skill's count on a page is n_p split evenly over its s_p skills (largest first), so 2–5 items (5 only on a 2-skill page of 10); over the sheet no skill takes more than ceil(N / 2) items. Skills are new to each page while the pool allows (k = Σ s_p distinct skills), then reused. N = 5 → 2 skills (3 + 2); N = 10 at M → 3 skills on one page (4 + 3 + 3). A pool of 0 or 1 skill is refused with its reason (§9.6).
progression: mixed (default): no two SHELVES of one skill side by side on a page (a shelf holds 2–5 cells of one skill); when every dealt skill on a page is one size class, the M1 arrangement interleaves ITEMS instead, with no two items of one skill side by side where the counts allow. The screen plays the printed order (§7a Order modes).
Order easy -> hard: by placement grade K..6+, then data.js teaching order.
Order by area: AREA_ORDER (CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS), easy -> hard inside an area.

drawing.sizes: Sizes M and L only (owner 2026-11-13; S dropped: a stored S or an S code reads as M through offeredSize). Look Daily (mixed-practice DEFAULT_LOOK); lattice Auto N = 6 at M, 4 at L. Shelves at most 7 at M, 5 at L (12.1 Mixed practice). Problems a page at most 12 at M, 10 at L (12.1 Review 12 / 8–12; DN-1: never over 20 at L), and at most 4 at M, 3 at L when the page's items are wide visuals (12.1 Wide-visual rows: number lines, base-10 over 100, coin rows). At most 3 distinct skills a page (12.1 Review: 2–3 instruction-led sections).

capacity.Ltypical: 1 (5); 2 skills — the 5 do not fit a half page

notes: *Typical* = shelves of 2 to 3 cells (stacks, equations, small visuals). *Compact* = facts and one-line equations. *All-wide* = number lines, coin rows, base-10 over 100: one cell a shelf, 12.1's 4 / 3 a page. "k skills" = distinct skills when the pool is large enough (Σ s_p; a page of 2–3 items holds 1 skill). A mixed sheet's real per-page count is measured by the engine between these columns.

pages = ceil(N / per-page); items split as evenly as whole shelves allow (largest page first, paginate.js rebalanced last page); never a page under half of another (H5); a shelf never splits (PT-MIX-9).

N = 5 prints 2-up (§9.7) when the 5 items fit a half page (M typical / compact, L compact): the same 5 items twice on one sheet, each half with its own header (Name, Date, Score ___ / 5) and numbered 1–5, a dashed cut line between; the key is 2-up the same way, each half numbered 1–5. When the 5 do not fit a half page (L typical, all-wide) the table's own pages apply.
The engine measures; the dialog never plans pages (L16). These rows are the targets the checks hold the measured pages to.
Key pages = pupil pages (facsimile, PT-KEY-1) + the key summary: under the last key page's grid when its rows fit (rows x 7 mm + 14), else one more key page. A week adds one weekly table page.

ownerRulings.ruling: A new paper type plus a playable mode, MIXED REVIEW: any mix of grades (school placement, chips derived, K-6+); any mix of the 9 areas with CCSS domain labels; optional untick of single skills; 'Only 8/10 skills' ON by default, read from redesign-passed.js; 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 25 / 30 problems; a seeded random mix with a 'New mix' button; every sheet has an answer key.

ownerRulings.ruling: Built on the EXISTING mixed-practice engine (sheet/roles/mixed-practice.js) and the review role (sheet/roles/review.js). No second engine.
SENDABLE: a share code / link reproduces the identical mix; it extends the existing share-code systems append-only.
PLAYABLE: practice card, online worksheet, quiz (scored) and the game modes.

All five improvements: (1) a Mon-Fri weekly set; (2) spaced / weak-skill weighting on screen; (3) the key and the results tagged by skill with a per-domain breakdown; (4) order mixed / easy -> hard / by area; (5) a 'From my lessons' pool.
Screens are print, computer / Chromebook 1280-1366 px and tablet 820-1024 px; no 390 px. Print sizes M and L only; S dropped (an S setting or code falls back to M).

misconceptions.error: Carries the last item's procedure into the next one (adds on a subtract item after an add item): the interleaving is the point; the cell's own sign and instruction must be visible in every cell (PT-MIX-5 cue), never only in a band strip of another skill
Reads item difficulty from position (easy -> hard order) and stops at the first hard one: the default order is mixed; easy -> hard is the teacher's choice
The teacher reads one total as mastery: the key summary and results split the score by area and skill so a 7/10 that is 4/4 place value and 0/3 time is seen as such

options: grades: chips K, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+ (multi, 'All'); a skill's chips = its school placement (the school grades whose pacing lessons link it) plus its data.js grade; 6+ = grade 6; default = the Skills screen's grade selection (mq_teacher_skills_ui), else Grade 2; each chip shows its pool count; a 0 chip is shown, greyed, with its count.

areas: 9 chips CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS, each labelled from AREA_LABELS (card areaLabels, exact): Counting & Cardinality / Operations & Algebraic Thinking / Number & Operations in Base Ten / Number & Operations—Fractions (decimals live here) / Measurement (Measurement & Data) / Data (Measurement & Data) / Geometry / Ratios & Proportional Relationships / The Number System (grade 6) / Words (maths vocabulary); default all on. MIXED and NOSTD skills are never in the pool (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R1).

onlyPassed: on / off; default OFF while the passed pool is small (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R6); the toggle stays visible with its live count, 'Only 8/10 ✓ (32)' = |pool before this filter ∩ REDESIGN_PASSED|; every passed skill in the picker shows a ✓ beside its name whatever the toggle; on = the id is in REDESIGN_PASSED (redesign-passed.js), read live.
skills: the pool list with a tick per skill; default all ticked; stored as an exclusion list (unticked ids), so a skill that joins the pool later is ticked.

fromLessons: off / 'unit' (this school unit to date) / '4w' (the last 4 school weeks) / 'year' (school year to date); default off; source = the school pacing (wrm-links allLessons() / unitLessons() + weekForDate), never pupil data (P-RV-9).
order: mixed / easyhard / area; default mixed.
week: off / monfri; default off; week number 1-40, default the school week of the first ticked grade (weekForDate).
New mix: a button, not an option: a new seed (freshSeed 100000-999999); the seed is shown in the teacher footer and carried by the code.
size: M / L; default the teacher's print default (printDefaults().size; L when unset, PT-DLG-5).
key: print on / off; default on; the key is always built, shown in the preview and reachable from the code (PT-KEY-1).

adapt (screen only): off / on; default ON when a pupil starts Mixed review on their own device, OFF on a teacher's link unless the teacher ticks 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1 token); never on print. This is the NAMED exception EX-MXR-ADAPT to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 (owner request 2026-11-14; lead ruling 2026-11-19, R2).

Not offered on this page type: look (Daily fixed), columns (Auto: the lattice decides), anchors / worked examples (PT-REV-2), arrangement (the order option replaces it), per-skill option editing in v1 (each skill at its defaults or its preset's values; ruling 8), Photocopy-safe and paper follow the job as on every role.

share.compat: Append-only: no frozen code, position or token meaning changes; a code with none of the new tokens decodes byte-for-byte as before (ws-code-snapshot, ws-share-options). An OLD app skips V / S / O / Y / K / P (parseEnhancedSkillCode's switch ignores unknown keys) and plays the same skills with the same weights as an ordinary mixed set: the skills survive, the identical items do not (stated, not hidden). The quiz host uses the existing ?quiz= share of a quiz built from the mix.
share.identical: Identical — one dealer: dealReviewItems(req), ONE exported function (in print-sheet.js, beside the duplicate ladder it must run: RETRIES = 40 and the rungs unique / answers / turn / repeat), takes the decoded request and returns the ACCEPTED item list [{categoryId, skillId, opts, seed, q}] in printed order. Its seeds are the formula: try r of item i = deriveSeed('mixed-review', S, day, i, r) fed to generateQuestionFor. buildSheet's mixed-review path lays out exactly that list (step 3 changes its seeding to the formula), and every screen host plays exactly that list — none calls generateQuestionFor itself — so print and screen match by construction, retries included. Same code + same release ⇒ byte-identical items. A later release that changes a generator may change numbers; the skills, counts, order and seed never change. With P1 the list is dealt on each pupil's device from their own record: identical per device, not across pupils.
share.frozenV1: Frozen under V1 (week and day codes): a week code carries the week's union with week totals, so a K<d> day is rebuilt by re-running the rotation. The V1 rotation (weekOf), the page-aware deal and the shelf-order function are therefore FROZEN under V1: any change to them ships as V2, and the V1 functions stay in the code so every V1 code keeps rebuilding the same days. MIX-REVIEW-SHARE pins a week fixture (tests/fixtures/mix-review/week-v1.json: codes → each day's skill list, counts, shelf order and item sha) that fails on any change. (Encoding each day's list in the code was rejected: the skills part's - grammar has no day separator an old decoder would skip safely.)
share.dealer: dealReviewItems(req), exported from js/modules/print-sheet.js: the only source of a mixed review's items for print and every screen host

week: Five sheets Mon-Fri of N problems each. Day d seed = deriveSeed('mixed-review-week', S, d). The pool is shuffled by S into a cycle; each day deals its k_d = sum of s_p skills (the page-aware deal) from the next skills of the cycle (wrapping); the rotation is frozen under V1, so every pool skill appears before any skill repeats; no skill on two consecutive days unless |pool| < 2 k_d; from Wednesday one skill a day is the comeback of a skill from two days before (spacing) when the pool allows. Print: 5 pupil sheets (tab 'Week n | Mon' ... 'Fri', footer code with K1-K5), then 5 keys, then one weekly key table (PT-KEY-5: areas and skills as rows, days as columns, item numbers in the cells). Each day reprints exactly from its day code (P-RV-13). One link opens the week with a day picker; a day link opens that day.
weighting: EX-MXR-ADAPT, the named screen-only exception to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 (owner request 2026-11-14; lead ruling 2026-11-19, R2): never printed, never sent, never a teacher record, OFF on teacher links unless 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1). w(skill) = 1 + due + weak, due = 1 when spacedRepetition[skillId].nextReview <= today (+1 more at box 1 or 2), weak = 1 when skillProgress[skillId].total >= 5 and mastery < 70; no record = 1; w in 1..4. w chooses only WHICH skills are dealt: it is the probability weight of the seeded sample of the k skills from the pool. The per-skill counts are the §2 deal unchanged (n_p split evenly over a page's skills, at most ceil(N / 2) over the sheet); w never reaches dealCounts. Read once at start (a snapshot); results go back through updateSkillProgress / updateSpacedRepetition. Keyed by bare skillId as progress.js keys it today.
breakdown: KEY: the facsimile pages (answers in the slots, item numbers as on the pupil page), then the key summary table (Andika, black and white, teacher type 11 / 12 pt at M / L): columns Area (name + CCSS domain code) | Skill (label) | Items (numbers) | Score ___ / n; one subtotal row per area ___ / n_area; a total row ___ / N. Under the last key page's grid when its rows fit, else its own key page. RESULTS (worksheet score card, quiz results, game end screen): 'By area' rows (area name + icon; screen chrome may use the area colour, PT-SCR-1) with correct / total and the item numbers, each expandable to its skills, weakest first; the quiz results extend the existing skillAnalysis with the area grouping. Per-skill and per-area subtotals always sum to N.
orderModes: mixed: across size classes, GROUPED shelves whose ORDER on each page is seeded (frozen under V1) so no two shelves of one skill are adjacent; items inside a shelf run 2–5 of one skill. When every skill on a page is one size class, the M1 mixed arrangement interleaves the items (interleave, maxRun 1 where the counts allow). The M2 block packer is not needed (§9.4). There is no separate screen order: the hosts play the printed order. easyhard: shelves and items by placement grade, then data.js position. area: AREA_ORDER, then easy -> hard. Numbering 1..N row-major; the hosts play the printed order.
lessonsPool: For each ticked grade g: the lessons of g's school sequence (allLessons() from wrm-links.js, the rows with grade = g, seq and weeks; unitLessons(g, unit) for the unit window) whose week lies in the window ending at weekForDate(g, today) → their WRM steps → the skills listed direct for those steps in data/curriculum/links/<YEAR>.json, plus skillsForWrmStep(step) (SKILL_WRM). Then the area, only-8/10 and untick filters apply. Outside the school year: 'year' = the whole sequence; 'unit' / '4w' fall back to 'year' with a note. No pupil data, no teacher records (P-RV-9).

checks.measures: A sweep (L21, L22): every N ∈ {5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30} × M, L × the 3 orders × 3 seeds × 12 seeded pools (one class, mixed classes, all-wide, all-facts, a 2-skill pool). On the MEASURED rendered pupil pages: exactly N numbered scored cells 1..N — for a 2-up N = 5 sheet, two identical halves of 5 cells, each numbered 1..5 with Score /5; Score denominator N; pages within the §3 table; no page over 12 / 10 problems, over 4 / 3 wide visuals, over 7 / 5 shelves, or over 3 distinct skills; mixed order: no two adjacent shelves of one skill (and, in the M1 arrangement, no avoidable adjacent pair of items); no page under half of another (H5); no split cell; the key has the same cells in the same places (PT-KEY-1; 2-up: each half 1..5) plus the summary.

areaLabels.export: AREA_LABELS, a NEW export of js/modules/teacher-areas.js beside AREAS; built by this lane (lead ruling 2026-11-19, R1); lf-checks and the lessons browser reuse it; no other copy of an area label string in teacher-*.js

labels.label: Ratios & Proportional Relationships / The Number System (grade 6)
No CCSS domain (proposed; the ruling did not name it — 1 grade-3 lesson)

areaLabels.poolChips: the 9 pool chips are CC, OA, NBT, NF, MEAS, DATA, G, RPNS, WORDS; MIXED and NOSTD have labels but are never in a mixed-review pool

rulings.q: AREA_LABELS is not in the repo (lf-checks has not added it; teacher-areas.js has AREA_ORDER / AREAS with 8 maths areas + MIXED, WORDS, NOSTD). Which are the 9 areas and their CCSS domain labels?
rulings.ruling: AREA_LABELS is ours to build: a new export of js/modules/teacher-areas.js with the exact labels of the lessons-browser card (card areaLabels); build-plan step 1b. The 9 pool areas are the 8 maths areas + WORDS; MIXED and NOSTD never in the pool. lf-checks reuses ours.

rulings.q: Weak-skill weighting reads the pupil's own progress, which PT-DLG-26 and P-RV-9 forbid for pages. Allow it on screen?
rulings.ruling: The weak-skill weighting is the NAMED screen-only exception EX-MXR-ADAPT to PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9, because the owner asked for it: the pupil's own device record, a start-of-session snapshot, never printed, never sent, never a teacher record, off on teacher links unless 'Adapt to each pupil' (P1). Named in PT-MXR-9 and in the PT-DLG-26 / P-RV-9 amendment sentences.

rulings.q: Role id: a ROLE_ALIASES entry mixed-review -> mixed-practice with input.review, or a thin roles/mixed-review.js wrapper?
rulings.ruling: Role id: a ROLE_ALIASES entry mixed-review -> mixed-practice with input.review (title, tab, supports level 1, exact total, order, fill off); no new module.

rulings.q: Order 'mixed' when the dealt skills have different size classes (the usual case across grades and areas): the M2 2 x 2 block packer is not built.
rulings.ruling: Order mixed across size classes: a shelf-level interleave (each shelf one skill with its band strip, shelf order seeded, no two shelves of one skill adjacent); the M1 interleaved shelves for one size class; M2 later, no format change.

rulings.q: Grade 'M' (Mixed levels) skills, e.g. the two vocabulary skills, and the 6+ chip: where do they sit?
rulings.ruling: Grade M skills sit under every chip their school placement lists, else under every ticked chip (counted once). 6+ = grade 6 skills.

rulings.q: The only-8/10 pool is small: 32 skills, all OA / NBT / Words (grade 4: 1 skill, grade 6+: none). With the default ON most area chips are empty.
rulings.ruling: 'Only 8/10 ✓ skills' defaults OFF while the passed pool is small. Every passed skill shows a ✓ in the picker; the toggle stays visible with its count, e.g. 'Only 8/10 ✓ (32)'. A pool under 2 skills is refused with its reason; never widened silently.

rulings.q: N = 5 is a short page (about 40 % at L): H5 says a page under half used is wasted.
rulings.ruling: N = 5 prints 2-up when the 5 items fit a half page (M typical / compact, L compact): the same 5 items twice on one sheet with a dashed cut line, each half with its own header, numbered 1-5 and scored /5, the key 2-up the same way; otherwise the capacity table's pages apply (wording corrected after card critic r1, D12).

rulings.q: Per-skill options inside a mix (a teacher who wants mult_facts 7s and 8s only).
rulings.ruling: Per-skill options in v1: each skill at its defaults or its preset's values; the code already carries ~opts.

rulings.q: Week sharing: one week link with a day picker, or five day links?
rulings.ruling: Week sharing: one week link (Y) that opens a day picker; the Copy menu also gives each day's link (K).

rulings.q: Quiz host: a new G letter, or the existing quiz builder and ?quiz= share?
rulings.ruling: Quiz host: 'Make a quiz' builds a one-section quiz of the mix's N items (each tagged with its skill), shared with the existing ?quiz=; no new G letter.

rulings.q: From my lessons: the default window when the teacher turns it on, and is the school pacing the right source (not the teacher's own plan)?
rulings.ruling: From my lessons: default window '4w' when turned on; source = the school pacing (P-RV-9).

rulings.q: Does the owner rule 'a distinct option is also a findable skill' apply?
rulings.ruling: No preset skill and no new tags: mixed review is a page type, findable as 'mixed review', 'spiral review', 'review sheet' in the print picker.

rulings.q: Should the pupil page name the area (band titles 'Place value', 'Time')?
rulings.ruling: The pupil page never names the area: instruction strips only; the key summary, footer CCSS codes and results name them.

rulings.q: May the teacher turn the key off?
rulings.ruling: The key print may be unticked (default on); it is always built, previewed and reachable from the code (PT-KEY-1).

rulings.q: Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, fromLessons off?
rulings.ruling: Defaults: 10 problems, order mixed, size = the teacher's print default (L when unset), week off, from my lessons off, only 8/10 off.

rulings.q: Signing: ws-spec-card has no page-type kind, so this card has no machine block and --check-signed cannot verify it.
rulings.ruling: The card stays hand-written (kind page-type) and is signed by hand; lane MR-E may later add a page-type kind to ws-spec-card and regenerate it.
